description: File Parser optimised for LLM Ingestion with no loss 🧠 Parse PDFs, Docx, PPTx in a format that is ideal for LLMs.

summary.one_liner: MegaParse is a Python document parser that converts PDF, PowerPoint, and Word files into a text format intended for LLM ingestion, with a stated focus on avoiding information loss.
summary.what_it_does: MegaParse loads documents such as PDFs, Word files, and PowerPoint presentations and returns their content as text meant to be fed to LLMs. The README says it aims to preserve tables, TOC, headers, footers, and images. It offers a default parser through a simple load call and a MegaParseVision mode that uses a multimodal model (such as GPT-4o or Claude) to convert the document. The README also mentions an API server, with endpoint docs at localhost:8000/docs after running make dev. It includes a benchmark script comparing its similarity ratio against Unstructured and LlamaParse. The README lists Excel, CSV, and text among supported formats in its feature list, but the support table only names PDF, PowerPoint, and Word.
use_cases: Parse Word documents for retrieval or RAG pipelines
Preserve tables and headers when ingesting documents
Use a vision model to read complex document layouts
Run a document parsing API service
how_to_run: Add an OpenAI or Anthropic API key to the .env file
Install poppler and tesseract on your system
On macOS, install libmagic with: brew install libmagic
Run: from megaparse import MegaParse; MegaParse().load("./test.pdf")
For the API server, run make dev at the project root
notable: MegaParseVision mode uses multimodal LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude) for document conversion
Includes a benchmark script comparing similarity scores against Unstructured and LlamaParse
Can run as an API server with endpoint docs
Targets preservation of tables, TOC, headers, footers, and images
caveats: Requires an OpenAI or Anthropic API key for the LLM-based features
Needs system dependencies installed separately: poppler, tesseract, and libmagic on macOS
README lists a 'In Construction' section with unfinished items such as improving the table checker and adding structured output
